method.model: ONE electrical load, explicitly declared by the inventor, that behaves as a single constant resistance R_load (in ohms) under ONE steady DC voltage V_load (in volts) across it. V_load is signed and is measured from the load terminal the inventor calls + to the terminal they call −. Under the passive sign convention (current taken through the load from + to −), the electrical power the load absorbs is P_load (in watts) = V_load × I_load with I_load = V_load / R_load, so P_load = V_load² / R_load: never negative for a positive resistance, exactly zero for a zero voltage and the same for +V and −V. The result is the theoretical absorbed power of that ideal relation only, not a measured, rated, maximum or guaranteed power and not a temperature.
method.executed_form: p_load = v_load^2 / r_load, with v_load in V (signed) and r_load in ohm (strictly positive, decided from the exact decimal value before any binary rounding); evaluated as the exact rational value of the two binary64 inputs rounded once to binary64 and accepted only when it is exactly 0.0 for a zero voltage, or finite, positive and within a relative error of 2^-52 of it; then shown only when it agrees with the exact decimal value V^2 / R of the entered values within a relative error of 2^-50, as that exact value rounded once to 12 significant digits (round half to even) and labelled exact or rounded.
method.derivation: DOE-HDBK-1011/1-92, Electrical Science, Volume 1, Module 1, gives Ohm's law, E = I x R (handbook page 14), and electric power, P = I x E (handbook page 16), with E the voltage in volts, I the current in amperes, R the resistance in ohms and P the power in watts (DOE-PWR-S1; recorded as electronics_electrical:PR004). InventorAI writes both with V for voltage, substitutes I = V / R into P = V x I and obtains P = V^2 / R for a resistance greater than zero; the handbook is not claimed to print this combined form or the passive sign convention, which are InventorAI's own statement. The relations are restated independently; no handbook text, worked example, figure or table is copied, no textbook material is reproduced, and the relation is not shown to describe the inventor's load.

rules: Grammar: strict ASCII decimal - an optional single leading minus, one to nine integer digits for V or one to twelve for R, and an optional single fractional part of one to nine digits; no plus sign, exponent, separator, space, Unicode digit, unit suffix, inf, nan or normalization. An omitted, malformed or over-length value is INVALID_NUMERIC_INPUT, resolved before the shared owner is called.

Representation limits, not physical limits: the digit limits bound what can be typed (|V| below 10^9 V, R from 10^-9 to below 10^12 ohm, steps of 10^-9); they are not physical limits, equipment ratings or a claim that such values are realistic, and the 64-character field cap is NON-PHYSICAL abuse protection only.

Positive resistance: the exact decimal value of R must be greater than zero, decided before any binary rounding; zero or a negative value is RESISTANCE_NOT_POSITIVE with no number. A zero voltage, including -0, is admitted and gives exactly zero power, never a negative zero.

Owner applicability: the shared owner declines an r_load that is not greater than zero as UNABLE_TO_DETERMINE / INPUT_OUTSIDE_ADMITTED_RANGE, shown as the neutral UNMAPPED_OWNER_OUTCOME (unreachable from the page).

Binary bridge: each admitted decimal is converted once to the correctly rounded binary64 value; every admitted nonzero value lies between 10^-9 and 10^12 in magnitude, so it is a normal binary64 number with a relative rounding error of at most 2^-53, a positive R stays positive and a zero V stays exactly zero.

Numerical acceptance in the adapter: the exact rational value v_load^2 / r_load of the binary inputs is rounded once to binary64. A zero voltage gives exactly 0.0. A nonzero exact result is accepted only when the rounded value is finite, positive and within a relative error of 2^-52 of it; overflow, underflow or any failed check is FAILURE / EXECUTION_INTEGRITY_FAILURE with no numerical payload, never rewritten as a refusal. Inside the representation limits every nonzero result lies between 10^-30 and 10^27 W, so neither overflow nor underflow can occur from the page.

Decimal-reference acceptance in the consumer: a successful owner result is shown only when it is exactly zero (not a negative zero) for an exactly zero voltage, and otherwise is positive and lies within a relative error of 2^-50 of the exact decimal value V^2 / R of the entered decimals; otherwise the outcome is KNOWLEDGE_UNAVAILABLE with no number. The proven worst case for every admitted input is below 4.0000001 x 2^-53.

Display: the accepted result is shown from the exact decimal value, never from the binary value: rounded once to 12 significant digits, round half to even, with trailing zeros removed; it is labelled exact when that rounding changes nothing and rounded otherwise. Plain decimal notation is used from 10^-6 W to below 10^12 W and the form m x 10^e otherwise, so a tiny nonzero power is never shown as 0. The digits shown imply no measurement resolution, precision or accuracy.

disclosure: This is the theoretical electrical power that one resistive load absorbs at the steady DC voltage V you declared, with the resistance R you declared: P = V² / R = V × I, where I = V / R.

Sign: V is the voltage across the load from the terminal you called + to the terminal you called −, and the current is taken through the load in the same direction. The load then absorbs P, which is never negative and is the same for a positive or a negative V.

The voltage and resistance are your own declared values. InventorAI did not measure them and does not check that the load is resistive, that its resistance stays constant or that the voltage is steady.

It is the ideal steady-state relation only: wiring and contact resistance, the source's internal resistance and voltage drop, temperature change of the resistance, start-up or inrush current, switching, AC behaviour and non-resistive loads such as motors, lamps, LEDs or electronics are not included.
The value is shown exactly when it can be; otherwise it is rounded to 12 significant digits and labelled rounded. The digits follow from your entry; they are not the precision of any measurement.

Next engineering need: this power is not a temperature. How hot the load or its surroundings become, whether the load, its resistor, wiring, source and any driver or switch are rated for this power, and what protection the circuit needs all remain unverified, and must be checked by measurement or a qualified person before any reliance. The result is preliminary, advisory, UNVALIDATED and not evidence.
